title: Signature Cost per Successful Task
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Cost, Latency and Compute Efficiency Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. The Signature edition does not copy any public product: it restates the subject in Manon's own Signature framing, as a design that lives inside the Signature ecosystem. Cost per Successful Task covers the following in Signature terms: divides total cost by the number of tasks that actually succeeded, not by the number attempted. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: an efficiency measurement fixes the task list and the success definition first, then records cost, elapsed time, and compute units per task, so that resources per successful task can be compared across configurations on equal terms. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: divides total cost by the number of tasks that actually succeeded, not by the number attempted. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo totals cost and time for a set of tasks and prints cost per successful task and mean latency. The demo program prints:

Tasks: 40, successes: 40
Cost per successful task: 3.00
Mean latency per task: 7.50 seconds

Use and limits

Efficiency figures describe the measured tasks and the measured accounting rules only. A cheaper run that fails more tasks is not more efficient once cost is counted per successful task. In Signature practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check inside the Signature ecosystem: follow the design, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this Signature database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here.

Record details

Record fields: resource: cost; task_class: retrieval of existing records; metric: success count; sample_tasks: 100 fixed tasks.
